design.pairing: every provider/model answers the same request back to back, so each comparison is between decisions made within seconds of each other
design.order: each iteration visits the corpus in a seeded shuffle; the provider order rotates with the position so no provider is always first or last
design.concurrency: 1: latency is measured one request at a time, so queueing on our side never leaks into the numbers
design.retries: none: the director and every adapter make exactly one provider call per request

smoke.purpose: wiring check; too few samples for tail claims

standard.purpose: median and p90 comparisons; p95 for a corpus of about 100 requests

full.purpose: p99 becomes reportable for a corpus of about 150 requests

sample_size_rule: a percentile p is reliable when at least min_tail_samples observations lie above it: n >= ceil(min_tail_samples / (1 - p))

metric_classes.measured: read directly from a call: latency, outcome, error code, reported tokens, reported cost, returned plan
metric_classes.derived: computed from measured values plus an operator-supplied input (a price table with a cited source)
metric_classes.descriptive: computed from the returned plans; describes behaviour and does not rank it
metric_classes.subjective: a person's impression; recorded separately and never mixed into a table of measurements
